exposure: Maternal vaccination status (COVID-19, influenza, pertussis, RSV)
cohort: The study included 1842 hospitalized children aged 1-24 months admitted with severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) in rural West Bengal, India, from June 2022 to June 2023.
finding: RSV and influenza were the key contributors to SARI in children under two in rural West Bengal, with RSV being the most common, and co-detection of viral and bacterial pathogens being frequent, especially in infants under 6 months.
